However several studies have shown an improvement in joint tenderness and swelling in patients with rheumatoid arthritis taking minocycline 200 mg od compared to placebo. Therefore, while it is not commonly used in rheumatology, there is a cohort of RA patients who remain on it. Option D - Infectious spondylitis: (also known as spinal osteomyelitis or vertebral osteomyelitis) is a bacterial infection of the vertebral body or intervertebral disc. Reactive arthritis may occur after non-chlamydial genitourinary infections or after gastrointestinal infections. Arthritis typically involves the lower extremities, the lumbar spine, and the sacroiliac joints. Incorrect Options: Option A - Gonococcal arthritis: The patient recently tested negative for gonorrhea, making gonococcal arthritis less likely. Gonococcal arthritis presents in one of two ways: (1) septic monoarthritis or (2) asymmetric oligo- or polyarthritis that may be associated with a syndrome consisting of tenosynovitis, dermatitis, and polyarthralgia. The prior often affects the elbows, wrists, knees or ankles. The latter is often associated with constitutional symptoms such as fevers. questions.solution: Correct Option D: Pulmonary involvement is associated with this condition This patient has dermatomyositis (DM). She has the characteristic distribution of the rash, muscle weakness with the presence of Gottron’s papules on the knuckles, and a heliotrope rash on the upper eyelids. DM is well described in children and adolescents. The Bohan and Peter classification includes 5 subsets of myositis: DM, polymyositis (PM), myositis associated with malignancy, childhood DM/PM, and myositis overlapping with other collagen vascular disorders. Pulmonary disease in the form of interstitial pneumonitis occurs in DM and PM in approximately 15-65% of patients. DM may be part of the antisynthetase syndrome, which presents as interstitial lung disease (ILD), inflammatory muscle disease, fever, polyarthritis, Raynaud’s phenomenon, and thick cracked skin on the fingers (mechanic’s hands). Dermatomyositis-sine myositis, also known as amyopathic DM, is diagnosed in patients with typical cutaneous disease in whom there is no evidence of muscle weakness and who repeatedly have normal serum muscle enzyme levels. Immunosuppression with glucocorticoids with or without intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), tacrolimus, cyclosporin, cyclophosphamide, and azathioprine may be needed.
